exampleAnswers.title: Calculating the Definite Integral of a Piecewise Continuous Function Given the Function Expression

question.text: The function $f(x)$ is defined below. What is the value of $\displaystyle \int_{-3}^2 f(x) \,\textrm{d}x\,?$ \[ f(x)= \begin{cases} 3-x, & x < 1 \\[5pt] 2x, & x \geq 1 \end{cases} \]
question.explanation: By the additive property of the definite integral, we have \begin{align} \int_{-3}^2 f(x) \,\textrm{d}x &= \int_{-3}^{1} \left(3-x \right) \,\textrm{d}x + \int_{1}^{2} 2x \,\textrm{d}x\\[5pt] & = \left(3x - \dfrac{x^2}{2}\right)\Bigg|_{-3}^{1} + x^2\Bigg|_{1}^{2} \\[5pt] & = \left[3(1) - \dfrac{(1)^2}{2} - 3(-3) + \dfrac{(-3)^2}{2}\right] + \left[(2)^2 - (1)^2\right] \\[5pt] & = \left[12 + 4\right] + \left[4-1\right]\\[5pt] & = 16+3\\[5pt] & = 19. \end{align}

question.text: The function $f(x)$ is defined below. What is the value of $\displaystyle \int_{0}^{6} f(x) \,\textrm{d}x \,?$ \[ f(x)= \begin{cases} 3x-9, & x < 3 \\[5pt] \dfrac x 3 - 1, & x \geq 3 \\ \end{cases} \]
question.explanation: By the additive property of the definite integral, we have \[ \eqalign{ \int_{0}^{6} f(x) \,\textrm{d}x &= \int_{0}^{3} (3x-9) \,\textrm{d}x + \int_{3}^{6}(\dfrac x 3 - 1) \,\textrm{d}x\\[5pt] & = \left. \left( \dfrac {3x^2}2 - 9 x\right)\right\vert_{0}^{3} + \left. \left(\dfrac{x^2}{6} -x\right)\right\vert_{3}^{6} \\[5pt] & = \left[ \dfrac {3(3)^2}2 - 9(3) - \dfrac {3(0)^2}2 + 9(0)\right] + \left[\dfrac{(6)^2}{6} -6 - \dfrac{(3)^2}{6} +3\right] \\[5pt] & = \left[\dfrac {27}2 - 27\right] + \left[6 -6 - \dfrac{3}{2} +3\right] \\[5pt] & = -\dfrac{27}{2} + \dfrac{3}{2} \\[5pt] & = -12. } \]

exampleAnswers.title: Calculating the Definite Integral of a Piecewise Linear Function Given Its Graph

question.text: The graph $y=f(x),$ shown above, consists of three line segments. Then,
question.explanation:
We divide the interval of integration into $4$ regions: the line segment for $x \in [-6,-4],$ the line segment for $x \in [-4,-3),$ the line segment for $x \in [-3,0),$ and the line segment for $x \in [0,5].$ Therefore, we can write the required integral as follows: \[ \int_{-6}^{5} f(x)\, \textrm{d}x = \underbrace{\int_{-6}^{-4} f(x)\, \textrm{d}x}_{-A_1} + \underbrace{\int_{-4}^{-3} f(x)\, \textrm{d}x}_{A_2} + \underbrace{\int_{-3}^{0} f(x)\, \textrm{d}x}_{A_3} + \underbrace{\int_{0}^{5} f(x)\, \textrm{d}x}_{A_4}. \]

  • The $1$st integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x \in [-6,-4].$ The corresponding region is a triangle below the $x$-axis, so \begin{align*} A_1 &= \dfrac12(bh) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac12(2 \cdot 2) \\[5pt] &= 2. \end{align*} Thus, \[ \int_{-6}^{-4} f(x)\, \textrm{d}x = -A_1 = -2. \]

  • The $2$nd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x \in [-4,-3).$ The corresponding region is a triangle, so \begin{align*} A_2 &= \dfrac12(bh) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac12(1 \cdot 1) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac12. \end{align*}

  • The $3$rd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x \in [-3,0).$ The corresponding region is a rectangle, so \begin{align*} A_3 &= bh \\[5pt] &= 3 \cdot 2 \\[5pt] &= 6. \end{align*}

  • The $4$th integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x \in [0,5].$ The corresponding region is a trapezoid, so \begin{align*} A_4 &= \dfrac12(a+b)h \\[5pt] &= \dfrac12(3 + 1)(5) \\[5pt] &= 10. \end{align*}

Finally, we obtain \begin{align*} \int_{-6}^{5} f(x)\, \textrm{d}x &= -A_1 + A_2 + A_3 + A_4 \\[5pt] &= -2 + \dfrac12 + 6 + 10 \\[5pt] &= \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{\dfrac{29}{2}}. \end{align*}

example.title: Calculating the Definite Integral of a Piecewise Linear Function Given Its Graph

question.text: The graph $y=f(x),$ shown above, consists of two line segments. Then,
question.explanation:
We divide the interval of integration into $3$ regions: the horizontal segment for $x \in [-4,-1],$ the sloped segment for $x \in (-1,0],$ and the sloped segment for $x \in [0,3].$ Therefore, we can write the required integral as follows: \[ \int_{-4}^{3} f(x)\, \textrm{d}x = \underbrace{\int_{-4}^{-1} f(x)\, \textrm{d}x}_{A_1} + \underbrace{\int_{-1}^{0} f(x)\, \textrm{d}x}_{-A_2} + \underbrace{\int_{0}^{3} f(x)\, \textrm{d}x}_{A_3}. \]

  • The $1$st integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x \in [-4,-1].$ The corresponding region is a rectangle, so \begin{align*} A_1 &= bh \\[5pt] &= 3 \cdot 2 \\[5pt] &= 6. \end{align*}

  • The $2$nd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x \in (-1,0].$ The corresponding region is a right triangle below the $x$-axis, so \begin{align*} A_2 &= \dfrac{1}{2}(bh) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{2}(1 \cdot 1) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{2}. \end{align*} Since the region lies below the $x$-axis, we subtract its area.

  • The $3$rd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x \in [0,3].$ The corresponding region is a right triangle, so \begin{align*} A_3 &= \dfrac{1}{2}(bh) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{2}(3 \cdot 3) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{9}{2}. \end{align*}

Finally, we obtain \begin{align*} \int_{-4}^{3} f(x)\, \textrm{d}x &= A_1 - A_2 + A_3 \\[5pt] &= 6 - \dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{9}{2} \\[5pt] &= \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{10}. \end{align*}

exampleAnswers.title: Calculating the Definite Integral of a Piecewise Curved Function Given Its Graph

question.text: If the graph of $y=f(x)$ is shown above, then
question.explanation:
We divide the interval of integration into $3$ regions: the arc of the semi-circle for $x \in [-6,-2],$ the line segment for $x \in [-2,2),$ and the line segment for $x \in (2,6].$ Using the additive property of integrals, we write \[ \int_{-6}^{6} f(x)\, \textrm{d}x = \underbrace{\int_{-6}^{-2} f(x)\, \textrm{d}x}_{A_1} + \underbrace{\int_{-2}^{2} f(x)\, \textrm{d}x}_{-A_2} + \underbrace{\int_{2}^{6} f(x)\, \textrm{d}x}_{-A_3}. \]

  • The $1$st integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x \in [-6,-2].$ The corresponding region is an upper semi-circle of radius $2$, so \begin{align*} A_1 &= \dfrac{1}{2}\pi r^2 \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{2}\pi(2)^2 \\[5pt] &= 2\pi. \end{align*}

  • The $2$nd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x \in [-2,2).$ The corresponding region is a right triangle, so \begin{align*} A_2 &= \dfrac{1}{2} b h \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{2} 4\cdot 4 \\[5pt] &= 8. \end{align*} Since the region lies below the $x$-axis, we have \[ \int_{-2}^{2} f(x) \, \textrm{d}x = -A_2 = -8. \]

  • The $3$rd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x \in (2,6].$ The corresponding region is a trapezoid, so \begin{align*} A_3 &= \dfrac{1}{2}(a+b)h \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{2}(4+1)\cdot 4 \\[5pt] &= 10. \end{align*} Since the region lies below the $x$-axis, we have \[ \int_{2}^{6} f(x) \, \textrm{d}x = -A_3 = -10. \]

Finally, we obtain \begin{align*} \int_{-6}^{6} f(x)\, \textrm{d}x &= A_1 - A_2 - A_3 \\[5pt] &= 2\pi - 8 - 10 \\[5pt] &= \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{2\pi - 18}. \end{align*}

example.title: Calculating the Definite Integral of a Piecewise Curved Function Given Its Graph

question.text: Given the graph of $y=f(x)$ above, find the value of $\displaystyle \int_{-4}^{4} f(x)\: \textrm{d}x.$
question.explanation:
The graph consists of $3$ parts: the line segment for $x \in [-4,-2]$, the arc of the semi-circle for $x \in [-2,2),$ and the line segment for $x \in (2,4].$ So, we can use the additive property of integrals to get \[ \int_{-4}^{4} f(x) \, \textrm{d}x = \underbrace{\int_{-4}^{-2} f(x)\, \textrm{d}x}_{A_1} + \underbrace{\int_{-2}^{2} f(x) \, \textrm{d}x}_{A_2} + \underbrace{\int_{2}^{4} f(x) \, \textrm{d}x}_{A_3} . \]

  • The $1$st integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x \in [-4,-2].$ The corresponding region is a rectangle, so we find the area using the formula \begin{align*} A_1 &=bh \\[3pt] &= 2\cdot 3 \\[3pt] &= 6. \end{align*}

  • The $2$nd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x \in [-2,2).$ The corresponding region is a combination of an inverted semi-circle of radius $2$ and a rectangle, so we find the area using the formula \begin{align*} A_2 & = bh - \dfrac{1}{2}\pi r^2 \\[5pt] & = 4(3) - \dfrac{1}{2}\pi(2)^2 \\[5pt] &= 12 - 2\pi. \end{align*}

  • The $3$rd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x \in (2,4].$ The corresponding region is a right triangle, so we find the area using the formula \begin{align*} A_3 &=\dfrac 12 \cdot bh \\[5pt] &= \dfrac 12 \cdot 2\cdot 3 \\[5pt] &= 3. \end{align*}

Finally, we obtain \begin{align*} \int_{-4}^{4} f(x) \, \textrm{d}x &= A_1+A_2+A_3\\[3pt] &= 6 +12 - 2\pi+3\\[3pt] &= 21 - 2\pi. \end{align*}
